task: Write one sentence of your own using the word penultimate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know penultimate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: In the spelling bee's penultimate round, four of the five remaining spellers went out on the same silent "p."
Late is the weaker marker — a late chapter sits somewhere near the end; penultimate pins it to exactly one before it.
Final goes further than penultimate: the final step is the end itself, one rung past the penultimate one.

Next-to-last is the everyday way of saying what penultimate says in formal dress: exactly one place before the last, no more and no less. Use it at the kitchen table; penultimate belongs in program notes and tournament commentary. The two point at the identical slot.

Second-to-last reaches the same slot as penultimate by counting from the end: step back once from the final item, one position from the end and no more. It never means merely somewhere near the finish — a looseness penultimate refuses just as firmly.

When a novel runs as a magazine serial, the penultimate installment carries a special burden.
It is the chapter in which everything must be put in position: the letter mailed, the rivals steered into the same city, the secret pushed to the very edge of telling.
Victorian editors called it the pivot, and they watched its sales figures nervously.
If the next-to-last number left readers cold, no brilliance in the finale could win them back, because half of them would never buy it.
Modern showrunners inherit the same arithmetic: the episode before the finale, not the finale itself, is usually the one that decides how a series is remembered.
